text: Follow-up (after 102.001-T lands): update the upstream spike/SKILL.md.tmpl in the external autoharness repo so regeneration preserves the in-repo docline findings-artifact fix (Principle IV, no out-of-tree writes). Refs: 102.001-T, 102-F, docs/exec-plans/2026-07-13-spike-findings-docline-reconciliation-plan.md.

Enable (or formally waive) the formal multi-persona plan-review skill gate. This environment cannot dispatch independent reviewer persona sub-agents, so Stage plans (091-S through 093-S) ran an honest inline single-agent self-assessment instead of the formal .github/skills/plan-review/SKILL.md gate (AGENTS.md:378 orders plan-review -> harvest). Establish a real persona-dispatch path OR a documented operator waiver so the pre-harvest gate is satisfiable and not silently skipped.

Add a labeled 'Constitution Check' section to the impl-plan skill output. Governance requires every implementation plan to map proposed work against the constitution; recent 091-S/092-S/093-S plans omitted an explicitly-labeled Constitution Check section.

OS-crash / power-loss durability for the size event+write path (out of scope for 099-S, Copilot G3). Both shared writers are sync-free: atomicfile.WriteFileAtomic (internal/atomicfile/atomicfile.go:15-63) does temp-write -> Chmod -> Close -> Rename with NO fsync before rename; events.EventWriter.AppendEvent (internal/events/stream.go:40-64) does O_APPEND write with NO f.Sync. So the 099-S event-before-write ordering guarantees PROCESS-crash safety only, NOT OS-crash/power-loss. Closing that gap requires a separate fsync protocol coordinated across BOTH shared writers (fsync the appended event file AND the atomic temp file before rename, plus parent-dir fsync). This is cross-cutting (changes the whole repo write path, not just the size seam) and must be its own release unit with its own review. Follow-up: design a repo-wide durability/fsync protocol for atomicfile + events.

Crash-window exactly-once size mutation, deferred from 099-S per Copilot cycle-3 H1/H5 descope (Option B2). Requires stable transport-visible OpID ingress on the CLI/MCP interface (SE-5 exposes none and no caller carries one), deterministic multi-orphan event-ordering, and a reachable offline doctor reconciliation routed through the real internal/core/doctor.go Doctor() workspace scan (doctor_target.go is single-file validation-only and is never called by the scan). Cycle-3 removed SE-3c (108.011-T) and narrowed SE-3b (108.006-T) to best-effort append-before-write audit ordering with fail-closed read (durable custom_fields.size is source of truth; orphan events ignored on read). Out of scope for a size-estimation feature; revisit only if exactly-once crash-window semantics become a product requirement.

Reconcile ship-gate descope exemption with canonical TerminalStatuses. archivedFromNonTerminalStatus (internal/core/shipment_gate.go) exempts a member from per-member F4 gate evidence when archived_status is recognized AND !isTerminalReleaseStatus. But isTerminalReleaseStatus={done,accepted,rejected,archived} OMITS shipped+abandoned, while canonical core.TerminalStatuses (blocking_cascade.go:14)={done,accepted,archived,shipped,abandoned,rejected}. So a member archived from shipped/abandoned is currently EXEMPTED though both are terminal. Decide the intended descope-eligible set (likely genuine in-flight {queued,active,blocked,review} plus possibly abandoned/rejected as descopes; shipped/done/accepted are completions and must NOT be exempt) and introduce a dedicated descope predicate for the exemption WITHOUT altering the other 5 isTerminalReleaseStatus call sites (shipment_lifecycle.go:250,271,304,326 release-progression). Add regression tests per status. Surfaced by Copilot review on PR #265.
